substeps.caption: Bruker S2 PUMA Series 2 with the XY Autochanger, its hood drawn see-through: cups of powder in the removable 20-position tray, and the grabber that takes them to the measuring chamber under the deck.
The grabber runs over the first cup and grips it (drawn as an XY gantry with a lift: Bruker doesn't publish the mechanism).
The grabber runs over the first cup and grips it (drawn as an XY gantry with a lift: Bruker doesn't publish the mechanism).
It lifts the cup clear of the tray.
And carries it to the chamber's port, which opens.
The cup goes down onto the chamber's ring, and the grabber lets go.
The ring lowers it into the chamber, film side down over the tube and the detector; the port shuts and the chamber fills with helium at reduced pressure, which keeps loose powder in place.

The beam, drawn see-through: up to 50 kV and 50 W from the tube; each element in the powder answers with its own X-ray lines, which the silicon drift detector counts. The tray stays free to load.
The spectrum: peaks at each element's lines give the composition, Na to Am, in minutes.
